decisions.why: The Latin closes the verse on the vocative Altíssime, a proparoxytone; the brief wants the last stress on the last or second-last syllable. Ps 9:3 (the same colon, psallam nómini tuo, Altíssime) moved the vocative to the head of the colon. Here the colon opens with 'e entoar', so the vocative goes inside, after the verb — which also keeps the Responsory's split (R. Bonum est confitéri Dómino, allelúja: * Et psállere, allelúja) whole: 'e entoar salmos' stands by itself.

decisions.why: The DO Latin has a comma: two nouns, decachórdum (Lewis & Short: 'a musical instrument of ten strings', citing this very verse) and psaltérium; the Greek ἐν δεκαχόρδῳ ψαλτηρίῳ is one instrument, 'a ten-stringed psaltery' (MS1932 follows that). 'As dez cordas' keeps the Latin's noun (the ten-string thing) in one short phrase and still lets the ear take it as the psaltery's strings — the Latin's two readings both stay open. 'Com o instrumento de dez cordas' is +6 syllables; 'decacórdio' is a dictionary word no one knows. 'Com' for in + instrument follows 32:2 and 48:5.

decisions.why: Factúra (ποίημα, 'a thing made') is a second word beside ópera (ἔργα) in the same verse, so it should not also be 'obra' (MS1932 merges them: 'com as tuas obras … com as obras'). The cognate 'feitura' is exact but is heard as Bible-speak or as 'the making of' something. The clause 'o que fizestes' keeps the root of fácere, stays apart from 'obras', and is how D16 handled a noun Portuguese has no plain word for.

decisions.why: Magnificáre → engrandecer (glossary). The Latin perfect passive (ἐμεγαλύνθη) says the works have become great; the second colon says the thoughts 'factæ sunt' deep — two verbs of becoming. 'Como se engrandeceram' keeps the verb and matches 'se tornaram' in the second colon. 'Foram engrandecidas' keeps the voice but is heard as 'have been praised' (by men). 'Como são grandes' (DRB) drops the verb. The colon is also the Sunday Vespers short responsory (Quam magnificáta sunt * ópera tua, Dómine): 'Como se engrandeceram * as vossas obras, Senhor' divides there cleanly.

decisions.why: 91:8 is a when-clause with no main verb; the Latin answers it with a bare purpose clause (Cum … : Ut intéreant — '[it is] that they may perish'). Portuguese needs the copula to make it a sentence ('Quando … : é para que …'); a copula is what D2 lets the ear supply. Without it the purpose clause hangs. MS1932 instead supplies a new verb ('imediatamente perecerão'), which changes the Latin.

decisions.why: The same adjective twice (úber: 'rich, fruitful, fertile, abundant' — Lewis & Short; from 'udder'; the Greek πίων, 'fat'), so one word for both (rule 6). 'Fecunda' fits both: MS1932 has 'velhice fecunda', and the fruitfulness belongs to a psalm of trees that flower and multiply. 'Abundante' is right for mercy but odd for old age; 'farta' (ubértas → fartura, 35:9) is odd for both; 'rica' would make the old age wealthy.

Sicut cedrus Líbani multiplicábitur) and as the Introit of Doctors with 91:14's 'in domo Dómini'; both orders read alone.

decisions.why: Bene patiéntes is a calque of εὐπαθοῦντες, 'faring well'; Lewis & Short give pati its sense 'to experience, be in a certain state'. A Latin ear can also hear 'enduring well' (a reading of patience is said to be Augustine's — from memory, unverified). Portuguese has no phrase that holds both; word for word ('bem sofrendo', 'bem pacientes') is not a sentence or says 'very patient'. The draft takes the sense the calque was made to carry, plainly and without adding (MS1932 'cheios de vigor' and DRB 'well treated' each add).

choices.91:2: confitéri → dar graças a (D5); psállere → entoar salmos (D25). 'É bom' for Bonum est (not 'Bom é'), the natural order. The verse is the Offertory / Gradual of several Masses and a Responsory (R. Bonum est confitéri Dómino, allelúja: * Et psállere, allelúja); it reads alone. The switch from 'Dómino' (third person) to 'nómini tuo' (second) is the Latin's and is kept.
choices.91:3: annuntiáre → anunciar (D41); mane → de manhã (row); per noctem → durante a noite (the nox row's build, singular here). véritas → verdade (row), not the Hebrew-based 'fidelidade'. Read alone as a Gradual/Alleluia verse (Ad annuntiándum mane …): it does.
choices.91:4: in + instrument → com, as 32:2 and 48:5; cum cántico → com cântico. The Latin's in / cum distinction is lost (grammar). The colon ends on 'cítara', a proparoxytone, as the Latin's ends on 'cíthara' — accepted as at 56:9. cíthara → cítara, psaltérium → saltério (rows).
choices.91:5: delectáre (causative, εὔφρανας) → alegrar, as 29:2 and 64:8 (the delectári row). exsultáre in → exultar em (row). The Latin's verb-last order kept in the second colon: it ends on an oxytone.
choices.91:6: cogitátio → pensamento (row; this verse named there).
choices.91:7: vir → homem; insípiens → insensato, stultus → tolo (D43; 48:11 has the pair: 'o insensato e o tolo'); intellégere → entender.
choices.91:8: apparére → aparecer; operári iniquitátem → praticar a iniquidade (row, = 91:10). The verse ends on a colon: its sentence runs into 91:9.
choices.91:9: in sǽculum sǽculi → pelos séculos dos séculos (D27); in ætérnum → para sempre (D23).
choices.91:10: The Latin's repetition 'quóniam ecce inimíci tui … quóniam ecce inimíci tui' kept whole, vocative and all. ecce → eis (que); períre → perecer; dispérgere (people) → dispersar, passive, as 58:16. Long verse, as the Latin's.
choices.91:11: cornu → chifre (row), exaltáre → exaltar (row: 74:11 'serão exaltados os chifres do justo'). senéctus → velhice.
choices.91:12: óculus singular → o meu olho (row); auris → o meu ouvido (singular, as the Latin). The tenses are the Latin's: perfect despéxit, future áudiet.
choices.91:13: cedrus Líbani → o cedro do Líbano (36:35 'os cedros do Líbano').
choices.91:14: 'na casa do Senhor … nos átrios da casa do nosso Deus' = the formula of 133:1b / 134:2 (átrium → átrio, domus → casa).
choices.91:15: senécta → velhice (as senéctus in 91:11; 70:18). adhuc → ainda (41:6b). ut annúntient → para que anunciem; the verse ends on a colon, its object is 91:16.
choices.91:16: rectus → reto; iníquitas → iniquidade (row), where the Greek has ἀδικία.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm91.txt (15 prayed verses, 91:2–91:16; no titulus, D7).

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps091.md. Hard readings: 91:4 decachórdum as a noun (L&S cites this verse); 91:5 factúra beside ópera; 91:8–9 the when-clause answered by a bare purpose clause; 91:11 misericórdia where the Greek has 'oil' (followed, rule 1), and the verbless second colon; 91:12 'hear' with no object; 91:15 bene patiéntes (calque of εὐπαθοῦντες). Liturgical pieces checked by grep in content/do (Latin): 91:2 (Offertory, Responsory), 91:3 (Gradual verse), 91:6a (Sunday Vespers short responsory Quam magnificáta sunt * ópera tua, Dómine), 91:13 (versicle; with 91:14's in domo Dómini the Introit/Gradual of Commune C4a, C5).

Draft 1: hard pass. Soft, all accepted: 91:2b +3 (the vocative moved inside the colon; two-word 'entoar salmos', D25's known cost); 91:3b +3 ('durante a noite' for per noctem); 91:5b −4 (Portuguese is shorter than 'opéribus mánuum tuárum'); 91:7b +4 ('estas coisas' for hæc); 91:9a +5 (the supplied copula and the reflexive 'se extingam'); 91:11a +3 ('como o do' for the genitive); 91:13a +5 (the article and 'palmeira'). 91:4b closes on the proparoxytone 'cítara', as the Latin closes on 'cíthara' (as 56:9). No rhyme flags.
